glance_takeaway: This page explains, for non-ML professionals, how modern AI image generators (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 3, Midjourney, Flux) work: a fixed process gradually turns images into noise, a neural network learns to reverse that, so every image is generated by denoising pure random noise — not by editing photos or copying a stored database. The many variants mostly exist to answer one question: how to take fewer denoising steps — from ~1000 naive DDPM passes down to 20-50 with DDIM and 1-4 with distilled/consistency models, with latent diffusion (~48x fewer values per step) making it run on consumer GPUs and a guidance scale (s~7.5) trading prompt adherence against variety. The forward noising direction is a fixed recipe; only the reverse is learned, and DDIM/score models/flow matching are one framework, not rivals.

F1.note: Hero figure (forward fixed / reverse learned arrows) + card 01: 'Generating an image means running the learned undo chain on pure random noise.'

F2.note: Card 01 detail: 'about T = 1000 steps ... predefined noise schedule ... statistically indistinguishable from pure Gaussian noise, like analog TV static.'

F3.note: Card 02: inputs = noisy image + timestep t (+ prompt, card 10); outputs epsilon / score / velocity, 'mathematically interchangeable choices.'

F4.note: Card 03 detail: random timestep, noise added 'in one shot: a closed-form formula', 'mean-squared error', 'no adversarial game as in GANs.'

F5.note: Card 04: '~1000 sequential forward passes per image. The steps cannot be parallelized' + 'nearly every major variant since exists to attack this cost.'

F6.note: Card 05: 'same trained network, unchanged ... deterministic ... 20-50 steps is the typical practical range ... only a modest quality loss.'

F7.note: Card 05 detail: determinism makes noise-to-image 'a well-defined function, so you can invert ... and smoothly interpolate.'

F8.note: Card 06 detail: forward = SDE, reverse-time SDE or 'probability flow ODE ... DDIM is essentially a discretization of this ODE', DPM-Solver ~10-20 steps, no retraining.

F9.note: Card 09 detail: diffusion 'runs entirely in this latent space' of a separately trained VAE; 'Decode the final clean latent through the VAE decoder — one single pass.'

F10.note: Card 09: 512x512x3 = 786,432 vs 64x64x4 = 16,384, 8x downsample per dimension, 'roughly 48x fewer values ... run on consumer GPUs.'

F11.note: Card 10 detail: prompt dropped ~10-20% at training, network run twice per step, exact formula 'guided = unconditional + s x (conditional - unconditional)', 'doubles the network evaluations per step.'

F12.note: Card 10: 's = 1 means no guidance; s ~ 7.5 is a common default'; caveat: 'roughly s > 12-15 in classic SD ... oversaturated colors and burned-in artifacts.'

F13.note: Card 07: progressive/adversarial distillation, consistency models 'any noisy point on a given trajectory maps directly to the same clean endpoint', 1-4 steps, caveat on quality/diversity cost.

F14.note: Card 08: velocity field, rectified flow = 'straight lines', 'a close sibling ... a reframing that generalizes, not a rival mechanism. Stable Diffusion 3 and Flux-class models are trained this way.'

F15.note: Card 01 fact box + card 11 myths 1-2: no images stored ('statistics, not copies'), starts from pure noise; memorization nuance box ('rare near-duplication ... exceptional failure mode, not the mechanism'); img2img/inpainting exception stated.

strengths: Perfect fact coverage: all 15 ground-truth facts are present and correct, most with exact representative numbers (786,432 vs 16,384, ~10-20% prompt drop, s>12-15 artifact regime, the CFG extrapolation formula verbatim).
Exceptional glance layer: headline sentence, three misconception chips, five stat tiles, and the forward/reverse noising hero diagram deliver T1, T2 (mostly), and T3 within seconds.
Honest visual encoding: the steps-per-family chart is a genuinely correct log-scale plot (bar positions verified against the axis), backed by a plain table carrying the same data.
Caveats are first-class citizens: tagged caveat boxes on distillation quality cost, VAE compression bottleneck, CFG artifact regime, and the memorization nuance — no overselling.
Strong wayfinding: sticky section nav, numbered cards with anchor ids, cross-references between cards ('the score from card 02', 'guidance card 10'), expand/collapse-all controls.
weaknesses: The guidance mechanism (T4's 'exaggerate the difference between prompted and unprompted predictions') is invisible at glance level — the CFG tile only shows the scale and its tradeoff.
The ODE-solver 10-20-step tier is missing from the glance tiles, so the T2 speed ladder reads as three tiers, not four, until Pass 2.

Most depth lives behind collapsed 'Full detail' disclosures; a 2-3 minute reader who does not click or hit Expand all gets skims only, and the chart's per-family 'character' relies on native SVG title tooltips with no visible hover affordance.
Rectified flow's '~20-30 (fewer viable)' step range is an editorial estimate not anchored in the source facts — defensible but the vaguest number on the page.
Information density at the top (chips + 5 tiles + hero + 12 cards) is near the ceiling for the stated non-ML audience; the layering rescues it, but a first-time reader could be briefly overwhelmed.
